newsitem.title: PERU: Shougang Peru pledges $137 mln investment to 2000.
newsitem.headline: Shougang Peru pledges $137 mln investment to 2000.

text.p: Peru's only iron producer, Shougang Hierro Peru, has formally pledged to invest $137 million up to 2000, principally to construct a new production line, general manager Raul Vera La Torre said.
He told Reuters the new line would double output of pellets to six million tonnes per year.
Shougang has committed itself to a timetable worked out with Peru's privatization board to invest $10 million this years, $27 million in 1997 and $100 million in the following two years.

Shougang Corp, China's state iron company, bought Peru's state-run Hierro Peru S.A. and its facilities at Marcona, 250 miles south (400 km) of Lima, in November 1992 for $120 million and a commitment to invest $150 million over three years.
Despite an initial commitment at privatization to invest $150 million in three years, the company only invested $34.8 million in this period.
"We are sure that we will able to fulfill the new accord up to 2,000," Vera La Torre said.
About 100 of Shougang's total 1,917 workforce have been on strike since Monday to protest low wages.
-- Andrew Cawthorne, Lima newsroom, 511 221-2134 REUTER AC
